messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] estimated variance by the delta or the variance propagation method in DSM
parts:
Isabella

Here is a sample summary from the variance propagation calculation:

Focusing upon the last two lines, the standard error is just as it it described.  The coefficient of variation (about which I think you are asking) is reported as a proportion, i.e. the ratio of the standard error to the point estimate.  Check this yourself:  328.3 / 1589.2 = 0.2066; CV(N-hat) is not reported as a percent.
